applies_why: This judge text does the thing the rule governs: it decides a collision involving the challenger's footed chain by appealing to Matthew 1:20's own words as decisive.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': one reading forbids using a single verse's own wording to resolve a chain collision, while the other allows a verse's own wording to answer a footed analogy; I used the first reading.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's analogy is footed but still uses Matthew 1:20's own words to reject it, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse move the rule retires.
